claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Controllers/AuthController.cs L11: `AuthController(DonHangDbContext db, JwtTokenService tokenService)`; L16 `db.Customers.FirstOrDefaultAsync(c => c.Email == request.Email)`; L17 `PasswordHasher.Verify(...)`; L19 `return Unauthorized();`. DonHang.Domain/PasswordHasher.cs: `namespace DonHang.Domain; public static class PasswordHasher`. API ref: Unauthorized() "Creates an UnauthorizedResult that produces a Status401Unauthorized response."

OrdersController.cs@stage-1 L21 `int.Parse(User.FindFirstValue(JwtRegisteredClaimNames.Sub)!)`; L22-24 builds `OrderItem` list; L26 `orderService.PlaceOrderAsync(customerId, items)`; L27 `CreatedAtAction(...)`; constructor takes `OrderService, IOrderRepository`, no DbContext. refs testing.md: "`CreatedAtActionResult` is analogous to a *201 Created* response with a `Location` header."

ProductsController.cs@stage-1 L10 `ProductsController(DonHangDbContext db)`; L16-18 `db.Products.Select(...).ToListAsync()`; L25 `db.Products.FindAsync(id)`; L26 `if (product is null) return NotFound();` — a null-to-404 mapping, not a business rule. No other logic in either method.

Placement vs behavior is supported by the repo: AuthController.Login queries in the controller and still works (seeded dev password, migration AddPasswordHashToCustomers). But §4 states as fact "With the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP), each layer has one reason to change" — SRP is a class/module principle; applying it to whole layers is the author's extension, and no pinned doc in versions.yaml governs it.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Layers apply the idea behind the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) at a larger size: each layer is meant to change for one kind of reason. HTTP details change the controller, a rule change touches the service, a query change touches the repository.
